page0.text:
...No, I shouldn't tell her.
This is my own problem.
I chose to keep fighting.

page1.text:
Zouken Matou and Assassin...
The black Shadow roaming the town...
Masters fighting each other over the Holy Grail...
I lost Saber in my fight to put a stop to all that.
...I can't lose anyone else.
From here on out, I have to fight on my own.

page2.text:
"Emiya...? Why are you all quiet?
Is there anything else you wanted to talk about?"

page3.text: "No, that's everything. I lost Saber, and I'm no longer a Master. We don't have any reason to fight now."

page4.text:
"Yeah. If you're going to forfeit the war, then that means we won't become enemies once our alliance is over... Bye, Emiya."
"Yeah. I'm forfeiting now. Without Saber, I don't have a chance."

page5.text:
I leave my seat.
I head for the exit, leaving Tohsaka behind.

page6.text:
"Bye, Tohsaka. Be careful around Zouken."
"Emiya, hold on—"
I open the door without turning back.
I leave the roof, as if to sever my ties.

page7.text:
The day ends.
If I'm going to trail the Shadow and Zouken, I'll have to start tonight.
With my lack of fighting strength, what I need now is a weapon and reliable intelligence.
I'll wait for night and then infiltrate Ryudou Temple or the Matou residence and look for clues.

page8.text:
"I need to look after Sakura too. I'll wait until tonight."
The war will continue once night falls.
Until then, I'll give Sakura my undivided attention.
...There's still time until then, so I'll pick up several days' worth of supplies on the way home.

page9.text:
"I'm home!"
I announce myself as I enter the house.

page10.text:
"...?"
But...
A sense of discomfort overcomes me as soon as I enter.

page11.text:
"Footprints?"
In the hallway, I see marks that look like footprints.
There are traces of someone tracking dirt into the house, while the house itself feels empty.
Only Sakura's shoes are out front, so the housekeeper I asked for must have gone home.

page12.text:
"Sakura?"
I go to the guest bedroom.
Nobody's inside.
Discomfort turns to dread.

page13.text:
I go back to the living room.
Sakura isn't here, either.
The tracks in the hallway end in the living room.
Someone with dirty feet did something here and then went outside.

page14.text:
I have a hunch.
Sakura was just here.
She was here in the waiting room, waiting for me to come home.

page15.text:
The dirty footprints belong to an intruder.
Sakura should be resting in bed, but she isn't here.

page16.text:
That's all I know.
It's strange that I haven't deduced the situation.
The answer should be clear, once I take some time to think.
Calmly.
Calmly.
Calmly.
If I calm down and think, I'll figure out what happened here.

page17.text:
But why...
"..."
Why won't my brain work at all?

page18.text:
I should have come home earlier.
I should have taken this more seriously.
Didn't I take Sakura in because I was afraid this would happen?

page19.text:
Zouken said that Sakura had nothing to do with this.
Why did I believe him?
As long as Sakura's one of the Matous, there's no way she isn't related.

page20.text:
So, why?
Why did I accept an explanation that was convenient for me, without questioning it at all!?

page21.text:
"..."
The telephone rings.
I mechanically answer the phone, my mind blank.
"Hello? You finally home, Emiya?"
Shinji's voice comes over the speaker, his tone pleasant.

page22.text:
"What did you do to Sakura?"
"Huh? Oh, I called you because I thought you'd be sad with her gone. You're really quick, Emiya. That's amazing. You figured this all out before I even said anything."

page23.text:
"Shut up. What did you do to Sakura?"
"Huh? I came to pick her up. She's my sister, so I can't leave her at some other guy's house."

page24.text:
"Shinji."
"Haha! Nice, you're getting pissed! I bet you're frustrated that I took her back!"
Frustrated...?
No way. I don't have useless emotions like that right now.

page25.text:
"Enough beating around the bush. Tell me what you want."
"Heh! I bet you know. Let's settle things, Emiya. I bet you think we aren't finished yet, after last time."

page26.text: "No, we are. You ran away. There's nothing left to settle."

page27.text: "You still don't get it! That was only because of the difference in our Servants, not you! I never would've run if you didn't have Saber! I never would've lost if Saber hadn't shown up!"

page28.text:
If Saber hadn't shown up?
...I see. It sounds like Rider hasn't told him that I lost Saber.
I don't know if she withheld that on purpose, but Shinji still thinks I'm a Master.
Yeah...that's why he came to take her back by force.
In other words, this phone call is...

page29.text:
"Shinji. What are you going to do with her?"
"Don't get all heavy on me, man. I won't do anything to my precious sister.
Not if you come to see me, alone."

page30.text: "You're telling me to fight you without Saber?"

page31.text:
"Whew! You're awfully feisty today, Emiya. Come to the school, all right? I'll bring Sakura if you come alone.
...Oh, but don't try anything stupid. Rider's Bounded Field is on the school. If you bring Saber, I'll know right away.
Of course...I bet you wouldn't do anything so cowardly in front of Sakura."

page32.text: I hear snickering over the receiver.

page33.text:
"I'll be right there, so wait. Don't lay a hand on Sakura."
"Sure thing. Come here as soon as you can.
You sure took your time getting home, though.
Can you believe this guy, making my precious sister wait?"

page34.text:
"What did you do to her, Shinji?"
"Nothing. It's actually taking everything I can just to keep Rider under control. It's just like that night. She's a real handful, and she's been looking like she spotted a tasty snack..."

page37.text:
There's no sign of anyone on campus.
School has been sending students home early ever since the mass comas spread.
Now after 5:00 PM, there probably aren't even any teachers still on campus, let alone students.

page38.text:
I feel hot iron enter my back.
I've already activated my Magic Circuit.
I focus on making my only weapon, Strengthening, ready to use at any time.

page39.text:
Is it Rider's Bounded Field, I wonder?
The campus is colored a deep red, and each breath hurts my lungs.
I cought violently, spitting blood.
Paying it no mind, I run up the stairs.

page40.text:
I have a feeling I know what I'll find, even if I'm not sure.
Knowing Shinji, he'll be waiting somewhere familiar to him.
He'll be in a classroom on the third floor.

page41.text:
I head up to the third floor.
The red filter only seems to darken, and I feel magical energy being shaved off me with each step.

page42.text:
Is he waiting for me?
I find Shinji watching me in front of class 2-C.

page44.text:
My mind goes white-hot with anger.
Is Sakura inside the classroom?
I need to make sure she's safe as soon as possible.
If Shinji's going to stand in my way, I'll...

page45.text:
"You're up, Rider. This is the Master of Saber, who cut you open! Pay him back for that night!"
A dark Servant blocks my path.
I don't care.
I can't stop, no matter who it is.

page46.text:
Daggers are swung at me.
I predict and evade them so quickly it surprises myself.
I move past Rider's left flank, avoiding an upward cut.
Rider doesn't catch me as I pass her. Maybe her long hair or stature makes that difficult.

page47.text:
I've got him.
I'm five meters from Shinji. I can close the distance in two seconds and target the Command Spell controlling Rider—
"...!?!?"
I gag.
Something grabs me around the neck from behind.
